correctness.rationale: The exterior derivative at \(x=ru\), for \(r>1\), is \(r^{-1}(I-uu^{\mathsf T})\); inside the ball it is \(I\). Segment integration proves the exact global derivative-supremum identity and the exterior limit \(r\downarrow1\) proves sharpness. The weighted maximum-norm operator norm is the maximum weighted absolute row sum. Cauchy--Schwarz reaches equality when \(|u_j|\) is proportional to \(w_j\) off the chosen row. The unique scalar optimizer of \(1-t+(W_i/w_i)\sqrt{t(1-t)}\) yields \((1+\|w\|_2/w_i)/2\); maximizing the row chooses minimal \(w_i\) and classifies all normal directions. The dual norm argument and matrix symmetry give the same constant for weighted sum error. The case \(n=1\) is checked separately. The 13,200 finite numerical checks corroborate but do not prove the universally quantified theorem.

value.rationale: For coordinatewise bounded measurement noise, Euclidean feasibility projection is globally worse-conditioned than its Hilbert-space bound suggests; the exact law quantifies all positive anisotropic weights in every finite dimension. The equality normals classify maximal amplification, and optimal equal weights show the unavoidable \((1+\sqrt n)/2\) growth. This is a complete natural quantitative stability classification, not an isolated numerical case or a relabeling of the native-norm bound. No claims are made for arbitrary convex bodies or higher-order conditioning.
